note: claude-opus-5-5、入力 2394 / 出力 2008 トークン

data.interpretation: The operator wants the shared road to be used according to ROAD_USE: fewer release-deadline overruns and fewer blocking_guard evictions. The direct measure is road_violations, which should be minimized. Two things are unclear. First, 'make sure the rules are kept' could mean a hard requirement of zero violations rather than simple minimization. Second, the violation count can fall for the wrong reasons, so blocking time and delivery performance should be watched alongside it.

options.label: Minimize road violations, monitoring real obstruction and delivery service

goals.text: Reduce the number of road-rule violations (release deadline overruns and blocking_guard evictions).
Watch that the actual time robots are blocked by stopped robots does not grow, so that violations are not just being defined away.
Watch that town-wide on-time deliveries do not drop because robots become overly cautious.
Watch that orders are not left undelivered at the end of the period.

options.note: Recommended. This treats the KPI as minimization. It adds monitoring so that loosening ROAD_USE, such as longer release deadlines or a weaker blocking_guard, or simply moving less, cannot pass as an improvement without showing up in blocked_s or the delivery numbers.

options.label: Zero-tolerance: road rules must be fully kept

goals.text: Reduce road-rule violations as much as possible.
Watch that real blocking time does not increase.
Watch that on-time deliveries do not collapse.

guards.text: After the amendment, there must be no road-rule violations at all in the measured run.

options.note: This reads 'make sure the road rules are kept' as a hard requirement. It may reject every amendment until full compliance is reached. It also creates strong pressure to loosen the rules themselves to hit zero.

options.label: Reduce actual road obstruction, with violation count as secondary

goals.text: Reduce the total time robots are blocked by stopped robots, which is the harm the road rules exist to prevent.
Watch that the number of road-rule violations does not increase.
Watch that on-time deliveries do not drop.

options.note: This assumes the KPI's real intent is a free-flowing road. It is harder to game by rewriting rule definitions, but it moves away from the literal wording of the KPI.

concerns: road_violations is a proxy that can be gamed at the rule layer. A ROAD_USE amendment that lengthens release deadlines or relaxes the blocking_guard would reduce counted violations without the road actually becoming better used.
Violations can also fall simply because robots drive less or wait more, which would hurt on-time deliveries and leave orders unfinished. The KPI says nothing about whether service may be sacrificed.
'Make sure the road rules are kept' could mean zero violations as a hard condition rather than minimization. A zero guard may block all amendments, or push proposals toward weakening the rules.

Numeric guards on delivery metrics were not set because no baseline values are given. If the operator wants a firm floor, such as a minimum on-time delivery count or minimum company on-time rate, the value needs to be supplied.
